rows.name: AI · one home — every door, one destination

content.title: AI · one home
content.intro: The same AI panel opens in two columns depending on which door you used: the inspector chips and ⌘J route it RIGHT with a “‹ Inspector” back row; the bare I shortcut and the ⌘K “Open AI panel” command route it LEFT with a close ×. Both can be open at once and each mount holds its own message list, so the thread you started from the inspector is invisible from the drawer. That is an IA decision nobody made, and it reaches the user as a bug.
content.decisionBand: One home — the inspector column, 300 wide.   ·   One thread — lifted out of the panel’s local state, so closing the panel, pressing “‹ Inspector” or selecting another element does not destroy the conversation.   ·   One shortcut — ⌘J.   ·   One palette row — “Ask AI”, always present.
doorTable: KEEP — the one shortcut. Taught on the sheet beside the chip.
KEEP — state the refusal BEFORE the prompt (UX-G-03).
KEEP — relabel “Ask AI”; the popover shares the panel’s state machine (UX-G-11).
KEEP as a shortcut into the row below — not a second destination.
RETIRE the destination. One palette row, always present, routing to the inspector column (UX-G-16).
RETIRE. The Panels group of the shortcut sheet drops “I — Open AI panel” in the same change (UX-G-15).
content.footnote: The rail keeps no AI button — AI is an inspector-column tool and RAIL_FIGMA is right to omit it. The keyboard sheet builds its Panels group from every tab that has a shortcut, so it will keep teaching “I — Open AI panel” until the ai tab’s shortcut is removed with the drawer mount: the sheet is an index of the decision, not a separate surface.
content.notDrawn: Deliberately NOT drawn: the left-drawer variant of this panel. A board for it would preserve the thing this decision removes. What replaces it is the row above — one destination, reached nine ways.

rows.decision: The AI panel lives in the INSPECTOR column (300 wide). One thread, lifted out of the panel's local React state so closing the panel, pressing '‹ Inspector' or selecting another element does not destroy the conversation. One shortcut: ⌘J. One ⌘K row: 'Ask AI', always present.

rows.name: AI · one mark, one verb, one contract

content.mark: One glyph everywhere: the lucide Sparkles icon, at the tier's own size — already the rail icon, the canvas-toolbar icon and the full-library alt-text icon. RETIRE ✨, ✦, the play triangle and the clock from every AI context: an emoji is not a design-system icon and does not respond to state, size or theme.
tiers: AI produces something that does not exist yet
Filled accent button. Opens a brief, then a review — never a one-click generate.
AI changes what is already here, and you see the diff
Bordered button carrying the mark. Ends in a diff card with Discard / Apply.
AI fills this one field. Nothing else can change.
Text-weight control in the field’s own row. Fills an editable draft; the field’s own commit is the Apply.
contract: GENERATING — Stop required. The user’s content stays on screen and stays valid.
PROPOSED — the diff. Nothing lands without this step.
APPLIED — one undo step per Apply, and an Undo button.
FAILED — Try again re-uses the brief, never an empty prompt. Discard and Stop leave the page provably untouched and say “Nothing was changed”.
typedFailures: “AI isn’t available on this workspace.” Exit: a route that can actually change that, or none at all. Never a settings page that cannot.
The server’s own limit and reset sentence, plus “Nothing was changed”, plus See plans AND “Continue by hand”.
“This is usually the model provider, not your site.” Exit: Try again, with the same brief.
The model answered with something this editor cannot map. Say that — never report success over an unchanged page.
rules: Quota is visible before the wall
A quiet “7 left today” beside the send control, amber near zero. ai.getQuotaStatus already exists and has no caller.
UX-G-04
Undo is a button, not folk knowledge
The applied chat message carries Undo until the next edit displaces it — today only the agent run has one.
UX-G-13
Auto-apply states the stakes, not the mechanic
“Steps change the page without asking. You can undo the whole run.” Privileged actions still stop for an explicit dialog, and the toggle says so.
UX-G-14
AI never evicts the surface that judges it
The diff card carries the live current value of every property it proposes to overwrite, so the inspector does not have to be off screen.
UX-G-12
Suggestions carry their own scope
A page-wide starter sets the scope to the page when clicked and says so in the band, or is hidden when the scope cannot serve it.
UX-G-19
Provenance survives the apply
Anything AI wrote is marked until the user edits it; the edit clears the mark.
UX-G-06
AI edits are findable an hour later
The transaction is already labelled ai-edit. Carry that label into the visible history, not only into a transient toast.
UX-G-20
content.flagFootnote: An affordance and the capability behind it share one switch. Brand’s “Generate with AI” renders unconditionally while its client is built only when the dsAi flag is on — and that flag is set in no env file, so the button is live for every user and the failure is the only reachable outcome (UX-G-07).

rows.name: AI · placement — what earns a door, and what must never have one

content.rule: A surface earns an AI affordance when (1) the task is repetitive typing or a first draft, not a decision; (2) the result can be shown as a reversible diff before it lands; (3) the surface can name the exact scope AI will touch; and (4) doing it by hand is measurably slower than reading and approving AI’s answer. Clause 2 disqualifies most bad placements. Clause 3 disqualifies the rest: if the user cannot be told WHAT is about to change, they cannot consent to it.
earnsADoor: Secondary — prompt popover on the selection toolbar
Secondary — the panel: conversation and agent run
Secondary — “Ask AI” on Typography, Colour, Spacing
Primary “Draft with AI”; bulk “Fill this column for 12 records”
Secondary — “Suggest fields” when creating a collection
not built — the command ships, the door does not
ships twice — unify on the vision path
title only, and silent on failure
Primary — one brief form, reached from both doors
ships as two wizards, one weaker
mustNever: AI may PROPOSE it — the propose → confirm-token → domain gate is exactly right. There must never be a “Publish with AI” button: a deploy is not a reversible diff.

Fails clause 4 — the diff is already rendered, structured and readable. RETIRE rather than repair. (Its procedure is NOT doorless: ai.summarize has an editor caller at useAISummary.ts:109. Retire it on placement grounds.)
Fails clause 1 — naming a checkpoint is three words the user types. A model call and a banner on a non-problem. RETIRE.
Settings · Domains · Redirects · Headers · Webhooks · Analytics
Fails clauses 2 and 4 — configuration with external side effects. A wrong DNS record is not undone by ⌘Z.
Customer data. AI must not read, summarise or rewrite it inside the editor.
Any affordance whose PURPOSE is deletion
delete-element stays in the vocabulary — a user can ask for it and see it in the diff. No “clean this up with AI”, no “remove unused”.
Fails clause 3 — a structural rename or re-parent across a tree cannot be scoped in a sentence the user can check before it runs.
The value of a client’s approval is that a human gave it.
owedFooter: 1 · “What AI can change”, in plain words, reachable from the panel. The command vocabulary includes deleting elements, moving them, rewriting design tokens, changing page settings, saving components and proposing a publish — and the user’s only view of it is whatever a given diff happens to contain. Plus an owner-level AI off switch at site level. Neither exists (UX-G-20).

2 · The onboarding brief — industry, description, location, tone, visual style, colour, reference sites — is used once at generation time and handed to nothing. Persist it on the site, give the editor’s AI read access to it, and put “Regenerate this page” in the Pages panel rather than on a wizard screen the user leaves once (UX-G-22).

3 · One honest index of what AI does. The dashboard’s AI-credits page advertises Content Generation, Design Suggestions and SEO Optimization as coming soon on the same page that meters the prompts those shipping features spend (UX-G-17); and one AI brief form serves both site-creation doors instead of a second, weaker wizard (UX-G-18).

rows.text: The panel's answer, and only the panel's. The message is honest and reachable — the server distinguishes this case with its own error code before it spends quota — but two other shipped AI entry points hit the same server error and show nothing at all: Pages → SEO “Write with AI” and Media → “✨ Generate” both swallow the exception, flip the label back and leave the field blank. This board is not the product-wide answer until those two carry the same two sentences.

rows.text:
V2 → V1 · History gap findings, closed 2026-09-07. No queue row existed for any of these.
UX-C-27 (Minor, carried from 06 · Content) — restoring persisted CMS bindings at load counts as an unrecorded change, so a freshly opened site disables Undo before the user has done anything, and the refusal names an action they did not perform. Restoring persisted state is not a user action: importing bindings must not mark history dirty, and any refusal must name something the user did.
UX-I-03 (Critical) — checked on the BOARD, not only in code, and on all 31 of its TEXT nodes rather than a sample. 163:113 draws no keyboard contract anywhere: no Enter, no Esc, no arrows, no shortcut line. Its only safety sentence is 163:166 “Nothing is written until Restore.” The Enter-in-the-search-box defect is therefore a code fact with no board that states it wrongly. NOT-APPLICABLE to this section; the code half is already guarded in the working tree.
UX-I-04 (Major) — panel half only: the drawer must say that time-travel is a MODE — “Time-travel is on. The canvas is read-only; ← → step the timeline.” The canvas half belongs to 09 · Canvas and 01 · Shell and is deliberately not drawn here.
UX-I-11 (Minor) — NOT-APPLICABLE, confirmed on measurement: 163:113 is a 360-wide panel board and draws no canvas-relative geometry, so the drawer's hardcoded left and right insets cannot be wrong on it. Carrying it would mean inventing a full-screen History board duplicating 1776:8385.
UX-I-13 (Minor) — the scrubber opens with the thumb parked at the MIDDLE of the stack. It must open at now, with the timeline running back from it, and the 163:160 “Previewing v3” label must then name the newest entry.
UX-I-14 (Major) — “Save this point as a version” belongs on every session row in this section, not only on the 163:158 link at the foot of the filter; the topbar half belongs to 01 · Shell.
rows.expect: V2 → V1 · History gap findings, closed 2026-09-07.

UX-I-29 (Major) — the approval band in 16 · History offers “Compare with current”, which switches the whole left panel to Review and opens Compare here. Corrected on a read of this board, 2026-09-07: 168:2 has NO back control to relabel. Its bar is 168:4 Compare, 168:12 Home ▾, 168:13 the change count and 168:14 ✕ — a close, which drops the user into the Review comment thread, a module they never asked for. What is owed is not a relabel but a named exit: ‹ Review in this bar, plus a second, conditional ‹ History › Saves shown only when Compare was entered from History. A cross-module deep link needs a return address and this one draws none.
UX-I-23 (Major) — NOT TOUCHED, deliberately. It asks to drop the “Opened · no reply” distinction; DECISIONS-OPEN §17 already settled that distinction as real, and this arc does not re-open a settled decision. The pill and bar boards live in 23 · Journeys · S-flows, not in this section. What is still owed is one vocabulary, defined once and consumed by the pill, the bar and the panel alike.

rows.text:
V2 → V1 · History gap findings, closed 2026-09-07. No queue row existed for any of these.
UX-C-27 (Minor, carried from 06 · Content) — restoring persisted CMS bindings at load counts as an unrecorded change, so a freshly opened site disables Undo before the user has done anything, and the refusal names an action they did not perform. Restoring persisted state is not a user action: importing bindings must not mark history dirty, and any refusal must name something the user did.
UX-I-03 (Critical) — checked on the BOARD, not only in code. 163:113 draws no keyboard contract at all; its only safety line is 163:166 “Nothing is written until Restore.” The Enter-in-the-search-box defect is therefore a code fact with no board that states it wrongly. NOT-APPLICABLE to this section; the code half is already guarded in the working tree.
UX-I-04 (Major) — panel half only: the drawer must say that time-travel is a MODE — “Time-travel is on. The canvas is read-only; ← → step the timeline.” The canvas half belongs to 09 · Canvas and 01 · Shell and is deliberately not drawn here.
UX-I-11 (Minor) — NOT-APPLICABLE, confirmed on measurement: 163:113 is a 360-wide panel board and draws no canvas-relative geometry, so the drawer's hardcoded left and right insets cannot be wrong on it. Carrying it would mean inventing a full-screen History board duplicating 1776:8385.
UX-I-13 (Minor) — the scrubber opens with the thumb parked at the MIDDLE of the stack. It must open at now, with the timeline running back from it.
UX-I-14 (Major) — “Save this point as a version” belongs on every session row in this section; the topbar half belongs to 01 · Shell.

rows.text:
V2 → V1 · Inspector gap findings, closed 2026-09-07. No queue row existed for any of these. Companion to 2866:21879 Inspector · OPEN DECISIONS.
UX-D-17 (Minor) — the footer's “N of M sections apply” cannot ever count six of the sections in a profile, because link, interactions, animation, element-properties, css-classes and all-css declare no CSS keys. The line understates every element. Remove it, or let a section report its own has-content.
UX-D-18 (Minor) — Visibility declares display / visibility / opacity / pointer-events and writes --hide-<breakpoint>. Declare the real keys so that applies, auto-expand and the footer count all describe what the section does. A labelling defect, not a dead control: the write is honoured end to end.
UX-D-22 (Major) — the raw-CSS escape hatch ships as CUSTOM CSS, an ordinary collapsed section for everyone, not behind a hand-set localStorage key; and the two Border implementations resolve to one.
UX-D-23 (Minor) — ID / Title / Tab Index is ADVANCED HTML, not “Element properties”. Hide it when it has nothing type-specific to say. The freed name belongs to UX-D-08's element editor.
UX-D-29 (Major · module summary) — the sequence is: the missing editors (UX-D-08, UX-D-09) → lock and multi-select (UX-D-02, UX-D-03) → findability (UX-D-10, 11, 25, 26) → collapse the two animation systems (UX-D-14).
Carried here from 06 · Content, because the binding popover 1707:8427 is an Inspector board: UX-C-10 (its dead end named a command-palette entry as the destination — corrected in place), UX-C-13 (the popover must ask WHICH property to bind, defaulted from element type and field type, and offer only fields that can drive the selected element; today every field type binds text content, so an Image bound to a Photo field never changes), UX-C-26 (+ Create Collection must return the created collection to whoever asked, reopen the popover on it and let the first record be created in the same flow, instead of abandoning the user in a wizard that auto-dismisses).

rows.text:
V2 → V1 · Publish gap findings, closed 2026-09-07. No queue row existed for any of these.
UX-E-15 (Minor) — ALREADY-CORRECT on the board, read back 2026-09-07: the footer of 1172:4825 holds 1172:4835 “Cancel” and 1172:4837 “Export as HTML” and nothing else. No Download All, no Download CSS. The three-unlabelled-buttons defect is code-only.
UX-E-28 (Minor) — OPEN DECISION, deliberately not drawn. The fix offers drop the row or replace it with the draft-share link; SPEC-PUBLISH-PANEL §3 deletes ENVIRONMENT as a section, and the draft-share link is owned by the dashboard. Relabelling the row would entrench a section the spec removes, and no IA edge is invented here. UX-E-31 (Critical · module summary) — one state machine with one publishable / not-publishable answer, one progress vocabulary shared with the worker, and a named way out of every terminal and stuck state; the topbar gate and the panel gate merge into one. Cancellation is NOT built end to end — no cancel check spans the Vercel deploy — so the cancelled state says “If the deploy had already started it may still finish. We will tell you which.” One correction the finding carries and this section must keep: on CMS detail pages the server DOES inject a correct per-path canonical and og:url. What IS the template's is the first title, og:title, og:description and twitter:* — that is UX-E-05, and the refuted half must not be drawn.

rows.name: note/Ecommerce · V2→V1 gap finding (UX-C-21)
rows.text: V2 → V1 · UX-C-21 (Major), carried from 06 · Content and closed here 2026-09-07. Dropping a product block offers to create a Products collection and promises it is ready for CMS data binding — then stops. It creates the collection and the sample products and binds nothing, so the block that triggered the offer still shows placeholder copy. Finish the flow: after 1719:8391 creates the collection, bind the inserted block to it and show the sample products on the canvas, which is the whole point of having offered. And make the offer recoverable — an action on the block or in the Content panel — rather than a one-shot prompt the user can only ever answer once.

rows.why: UX-I-38 (Major, dead-end) — LockedScreen takes a per-screen `message` prop (LockedScreen.tsx:36,58) and nothing passes one. settings-text.json guarded this row on 'Upgrade your plan to unlock this feature.'; a full TEXT read of 1138:13436 shows that string is NOT on the board. What is on it is worse and nobody had filed it: the CUSTOM CODE locked screen is titled 'Custom code is a Pro feature' and then describes a different feature — 'Set CSP, HSTS and frame policy on your own domain', which is the Headers screen's subject. The locked door is not merely unlabelled, it is labelled with the wrong room. `width` is set because the node is WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT and would otherwise grow to a single ~1000px line.

rows.name: Rail · selected vs open (two signals) — UX-F-02: selected and open are two signals, not one. aria-selected and the accent bar are both bound to “active AND drawer open” (LeftSidebar.tsx:137-160), so with the drawer shut the rail reports a tablist with nothing chosen. The selected item stays marked whether the drawer is open or shut, and rail arrow-keys either move focus only (manual activation) or open the panel they select. Specimen still owed: 199:409 Shell state 5 · Drawer closed draws a fully neutral rail, so the file agrees with the code's bug rather than with this board.

rows.detail: UX-D-04 — OPEN-DECISION. Already drawn, not re-drawn. Board 2866:21879 “Inspector · OPEN DECISIONS (V2 → V1)”, body TEXT 2866:21881 (672x533 @24,56, parents 2866:21879:FRAME > 1776:8381:SECTION), decision 4 read back verbatim this pass: “OPEN (UX-D-04). Either way the reach is a working MODE…”. It states both admissible answers — scope the peer set to the active page so the existing copy becomes true, or keep it project-wide and say so with a way to see the peers first — and names the code: getAllElements() is every registered element across all loaded pages (ElementManager.ts:151-158), cleared only by a full project reset (:530-533), while ScopeDropdown.tsx:153,159 says “on this page”. A second board restating this would fork it.

rows.detail: UX-E-05 — IMPLEMENTED-AS-RULE. The note already carried the correction; this pass added the FIX. Appended to 2876:12480 note/Publish (section 1776:8378) and read back OK, 108 -> 144px: replace the generated page's head identity rather than appending to it — one <title>, one meta description, one og:title / og:description / twitter:* derived from the entry, template head removed first (cms.service.ts:206-215) — and the collection's page-generation settings show one real entry's rendered head before publish. The head-preview card is NOT drawn, and that is now a measurement rather than a guess. publish-crosssection#10 carried this arc's last unresolved selector; it resolves to 2429:12111 “Content · dynamic-pages” (280x812 @2320,220 in 1776:8376), read this pass: layoutMode=VERTICAL and contentExtent=812 of 812 — the board is FULL, so a head-preview section can only be added by hiding rows that carry other findings' content. Its three sibling states (2429:21243 no-pattern, 2429:21262 none-published, 2429:21281 no-template) are all 280x812 and equally full, as are 2850:12042 unknown-key and 2850:21351 no-records. A new board is no cheaper: section 06 · Content measures 3440x5957 with maxBottom=5927, a free strip of THIRTY pixels, and the section already computes as a pre-existing overlap against 07 · Brand — growing it makes that overlap worse. So the card wants a section re-space (order-sections.mjs), which is the arrangement lane's job and not something to start while other passes write into the same file. rows.why: UX-G-03
rows.detail: UX-G-03 — IMPLEMENTED. The board exists and its interior carries the fix; both facts needed a read, because add-board rows never reach queue-state and the previous AI pass asserted existence without opening it. Board 2846:21654 “AI · scoped-multi” (280x812 @940,220 in 1776:8380, rx=1 so it is reachable) reads back five TEXT nodes: 2846:21660 “Scope: 3 selected”, 2846:21665 “AI edits ONE element at a time in v1. The composer is disabled while more than one element is select…”, and 2846:21663 “Select one element to use AI here” as the disabled composer placeholder. That is the finding's preferred fix exactly — the refusal stated up front, before the prompt, by the scope band that already knows the answer — rather than the shipped behaviour of refusing after the user types (toServerScope returns null for “multi”, useStreamPrompt.ts:47-51; AITab.tsx:82-93 pushes the refusal without calling the server).

rows.why: UX-G-23
rows.detail: UX-G-23 — IMPLEMENTED. Read back on all three blocked states this pass, which is what the previous AI pass could not do (build-ai-v2-boards step D returned SKIP-EXISTS, a string match carrying no node id and therefore not evidence). The manual route is present as the second action on each: 171:105 “AI · error-quota” carries 2846:21651 “Continue by hand in the inspector” at @16,104 beside 171:135 “See plans”; 171:136 “AI · not-configured” carries 2846:21649 at @16,138; and 2846:21667 “AI · error-provider” carries 2846:21681 at @16,104 beside 2846:21680 “Try again”. The finding's other half is stated on the same board at 2846:21682: “The thread and the prompt you typed stay on screen behind this state. Losing the user's words is a s…”. The one sliver NOT drawn is “open billing in-place with a return”: 171:135 “See plans” carries no in-place statement, and adding one would re-layout a 280x812 board whose child ids were never read.

rows.why: UX-A-07 (Major, broken-flow)
rows.name: caption/UX-A-07 · the onboarding step and this panel disagree
rows.text: The onboarding checklist says “Drop a ready-made section — hero, features, footer — onto the canvas” and its button opens this panel. Hero and features are not element rows: they exist only inside BLOCKS, which is COLLAPSED by default and sits below 53 element rows. Either put the section-shaped blocks where the step points — a SECTIONS group open by default, or hero/features promoted into the first screenful, droppable — or rewrite the step to name something the panel actually offers on open. The taxonomy above is founder-final (blocks/groups.ts:1-19), so this is a board decision, not a silent rename.

rows.why: UX-B-31 (Major, missing-screen)
rows.name: caption/UX-B-31 · there is no recently-deleted
rows.text: Deleted pages are recoverable only through Undo, and Undo is the single editor-wide history stack — a page deleted and then followed by three canvas edits needs four undos, which also throw away those three edits. The confirm dialog names ⌘Z as the way back and it is honest only for the case where nothing has happened since. Keep deleted pages recoverable for a session INDEPENDENTLY of the undo stack, reachable from this panel. No such screen exists anywhere in the file.

rows.why: UX-I-33 (Critical, destructive-confirm)
rows.name: caption/UX-I-33 · deleting a redirect has no confirm
rows.text: Deleting a redirect fires the server mutation on the first click — no confirm, no undo, no toast, and the only feedback is the row disappearing. A redirect is a live routing rule that search engines and existing inbound links depend on. Confirm, naming the rule and what breaks: “/old-pricing will start returning 404.” An undo window on the row would be better still.

rows.name: Layers · locked — TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH — the padlock is drawn from a per-page localStorage set; the lock the canvas enforces is ElementData.locked on the document. rows.text: 28h dense rows. At depth 5 the name gets 96px: 280 − 92 indent − 12 chevron − 12 icon − 4×8 gaps − 30 for the two toggles − 6 right pad. The long row here is the stress case. A row shows a custom name, else the element’s own first 32 characters, else the type label. Arrow keys move the selection, never focus — Down twice selects the same row twice, so the tree cannot be walked (LayerTreeItem.tsx:155-164). Every row is its own tab stop plus up to three more (:172). The eye and lock are 20px tall with no width set — about 15×20, under the 24×24 pointer minimum this 28h row can afford (layers-v2.css:157-178). The M/T breakpoint badges here can never render: buildTree returns five fields and never breakpointOverrides (useLayerTree.ts:88-95). Hidden and locked have no roll-up — the footer counts total and selected only, and search matches name, type, tag and id, not state (LayersTab.tsx:216-221, useLayerSearch.ts:16-24).

rows.why: UX-H-24
rows.text: The line is drawn over illegal targets too — the drop is what refuses, not the hover. The reason appears as an alert at the top of the panel and clears itself after 3s. The reason is built from raw type ids — “button cannot contain children”, “text cannot be nested inside heading” — not the names on the rows, and a locked container refuses the drop with no locked-target affordance during the drag (index.tsx:87-93, 120-160).
rows.expect: The line is drawn over illegal targets too

rows.why: UX-H-17
rows.text: Hidden is not deleted. 45% opacity, keeps its place in the tree. Dimming opens no undo step, so ⌘Z undoes your previous edit instead and the dim stays on — and it is stored in this browser only, so a collaborator does not see it. The glyph is an eye, the universal symbol for hide, on a control that hides nothing; the control that does is the Inspector’s Visibility section, and the two have no visible relationship (LayerTreeItem.tsx:285-306).

rows.why: UX-H-14 (Critical) + UX-H-15
rows.text: Locked has no row treatment: no dim, no tint. The only signals are the darker padlock, the aria-label suffix and draggable=false (LayerTreeItem.tsx:99, layers-v2.css has no locked rule). Lock is written to TWO places that never reconcile — a per-page localStorage set the panel re-reads, and ElementData.locked on the document, which is what the canvas enforces. hydrateFromStorage pushes storage INTO the engine and never reads element.isLocked() back, so on a second machine or after clearing site data the padlock draws OPEN while the canvas refuses the element and says “This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.” — naming the one control that is showing the opposite state (useLayerActions.ts:70-97,163-168; Element.ts:151-155; useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95). And the lock only holds on one of the two surfaces: clicking this row selects the element normally and the Inspector edits it (useLayerSelection.ts:68-74).

rows.text:
V2 UX-H-33 — THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: Media has two surfaces with unequal powers. This 280 drawer is the default (MediaTab → SlimLauncher, mounted at 320); the fullpage LibraryManager holds rename, folders, sort, single-asset delete, the richer stock browser and the per-asset context menu. Nothing in the drawer named the second one or explained why an action was missing. This pass closes the gap in the drawer where the code already can (Select, the folder menu with ＋ New folder, the four footer doors, rename/copy-URL/download/delete on the drill-in) and names the destination for the rest in the footer's second line. Decision recorded, NOT taken: make one surface canonical and the other a size of it.

OPEN DECISION — the drawer has three widths and no token. This board draws 280. The panel mounts at 320 (SlimLauncher). LeftSidebar.css:231 overrides Media to 560, which V2 §11 measured and called 'a runtime override with no token'. The expanded drawer elsewhere is 700 (LeftSidebar.tsx:586-587), and SPEC-NAVIGATION proposes 560 while SPEC-PAGES-PANEL and SPEC-PUBLISH-PANEL draw 700. Not resolved here; the brief says draw 700 for the expanded drawer and file the 560 proposal as an open decision.

V2 UX-H-04 — there are TWO stock browsers with different powers and which one you get depends on which Media surface you opened. This 280 overlay can only SAVE into the library; you must then find the asset in the grid and click it again to place it (StockBrowserOverlay.tsx:148, props :26-38 carry no onInsert). The 720 StockSourceModal can insert straight onto the canvas, switch provider, filter by colour and browse icons and fonts (MediaTab.tsx:232-255). Nothing tells the user the other exists. Recommendation: one component, two sizes, same actions.

V2 UX-H-03 — the overlay is not wired to the failure flag at all: MediaTab.tsx:378-392 passes no searchFailed and StockBrowserOverlayProps declares none, while :243 passes one to the modal. Its three result states are now boarded separately (no-results / search-failed / not-configured).

V2 UX-H-12 — an upload in flight could not be cancelled or dismissed: UploadZone.tsx:163-192 renders a name, a percent and a bar and no control at all, and state.dismissUpload is wired only in the fullpage manager (LibraryManager.tsx:379). A 48 MB video picked by accident occupied the footer until it finished or failed. Cancel added here, dismiss on the failed sibling.

rows.why: UX-H-06 + the owed pre-upload rejection state.
rows.text:
V2 UX-H-06 — the file picker offered more formats than the product can store: UploadZone.tsx:15 accepts image/*,video/* so an iPhone HEIC, an .avi and an .mkv all start uploading, and the server's allow-list is a closed set of eight media formats plus fonts (app/api/asset-upload/route.ts:31-49). The limit on this row is now the one the code enforces — 50 MB per file (UploadZone.tsx:16, route.ts:52), not the picker's 10 MB (MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:272), which remains unreconciled.

Still missing: the PRE-upload rejection state — the red strip UploadZone.tsx:55-73 flashes for 4000ms with its two reasons — has no board (W-A-42).

V2 UX-H-10 — the one screen entirely about a single file offered no rename, no delete, no download and no copy-URL; its five rows were Used in / Versions / Edit image / Optimise / Replace across site (AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:415-465), while useMediaState.ts:379-381 exports renameItem and copyUrl to no consumer at all. Four rows added. Combined with UX-H-01 this is why a user who opened a file in the drawer and wanted it gone had to leave for the fullpage manager.

V2 UX-H-09 — ✨ Generate fails in total silence: AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:270-289's catch body is a comment, so unconfigured, out-of-credit, rate-limited and provider-down are indistinguishable from 'the AI had nothing to say'. See the alt-generate-failed state board.

V2 UX-H-01 — this state used to be entered by right-clicking an asset, a gesture the drawer stole from the per-asset menu (SlimLauncher.tsx:469-476 → MediaTab.tsx:352-355). Bulk selection now has its own ☑ Select control in the folder row, and right-click opens the menu MediaContextMenu.tsx already implements and MediaTab.tsx:16 imports without ever rendering.

V2 UX-H-07 — the drawer's folder scope button was disabled whenever the library had no folders (SlimLauncher.tsx:255) and the drawer had no way to create one; folder creation lived only in the fullpage folder rail (LibraryManager.tsx:354, FolderTree.tsx:378). ＋ New folder… now sits in the drawer's own 📁 All ▾ menu.

SINGLE OWNER (UX-I-19): this confirm is the only re-send path in the design. The ReviewBar's Re-send sits under the topbar the whole time a round is live and fires straight through with no confirm at all (ReviewBar.tsx:148-159). It routes here, or it goes. Two live affordances for one irreversible action is the condition this confirm exists to prevent.

rows.why: UX-I-22 (role) and UX-I-26 (reply target) both land on the panel's work surface. Record both on the root state's caption.
rows.text: The wedge's work surface. It answers one question: what do I still owe the client before I re-send? Progress 44h is the number that decides that. Comments group by page because fixing is page-by-page work. n / p jump to next and previous open comment without leaving the canvas. ROLE (UX-I-22): every mutating control here — Resolve, Reopen, Reattach, Revoke, Re-send — renders live for a VIEWER and is refused by the server after the click. The panel already computes the role and spends it in one place only, Send for review's disabled reason (ReviewTab.tsx:146,479). Same named-reason treatment on all of them; the shut state is drawn on 'Review panel · viewer — read-only'. REPLY (UX-I-26): one composer at the foot posts against comments[0].pageId, so an answer to the third comment lands on the first comment's page.

rows.why: UX-I-25 — the strip reads as broken navigation. The fix is honesty, not a feature: label it a log and strip the row affordances.
rows.text: Read-only. Without round history, round 3 cannot see rounds 1 and 2, and a client who repeats feedback looks unreasonable when they are not. LOG, NOT NAVIGATION (UX-I-25): the rows are spans and open nothing — comments carry no round id, so an older round's comments are not retrievable at all (ReviewTab.tsx:743-790). Title the strip 'Round history', and give the rows no hover, no chevron and no row fill, so it reads as a record of outcomes rather than a list of destinations. Carrying a round id on comments is the other answer, and it is a schema change, not a redraw.

rows.why: UX-I-28 (no position in the comment walk) and VIS-1-16 (the round pager wraps 'Round 3 of 3' mid-word into a ~40px box) are the same control failing two ways. Record both on the board that draws the pager.
rows.text: 12 of 12. Re-send is not gated on this — you can send with comments open — but reaching it is the normal exit. PAGER (VIS-1-16 / UX-I-28): the round pager between the two chevrons is about 40px wide and wraps 'Round 3 of 3' mid-word to three lines. Widen the label box so the position prints on one line. The comment walk needs the same thing: ReviewBar's 'Next ›' steps the open comments modulo their length and never says where you are (ReviewBar.tsx:88-102) — print '3 of 7', add a Prev step, and mark visited comments so the walk has an end.
rows.expect: 12 of 12. Re-send is not gated on this

rows.why: UX-I-21 (Compare is a full-surface job, not a 280 drawer job; one header, not two) and UX-I-20 (Compare ends nowhere). The §17 boards are already drawn 1080 wide — the canvas surface — which IS the recommendation; the caption must say so, because the code still mounts Compare in the drawer.
rows.text: Two independent panes. Left is the approved snapshot, right is the site as it is now. Each pane is a sandboxed frame and nothing syncs them — the labels carry the asymmetry, not colour. (A third mode, List, shows the same comparison as rows.) SURFACE (UX-I-21): these boards are drawn 1080 wide — the canvas surface, 1440 less the 60 rail and the 300 inspector — not the drawer the code mounts Compare in today (ReviewTab.tsx:497-532; --bk-size-drawer 280, expanded 700). Two full web pages at about 130px a pane is not a comparison. Compare opens on the canvas surface, the way Settings already does with mode: fullpage. ONE header, not two: the inner toolbar currently replaces the panel header and takes the expand, close and help controls off the one screen that needs them. ENDING (UX-I-20): Compare is read-only and stops. It ends on a decision — see the footer.

rows.why: UX-I-27 — every change row is a plain div. Make a row a destination.
rows.text: No render at all — just what moved. The fastest of the three when you only need the inventory. DESTINATION (UX-I-27): every change row is a plain div today — 'Added', 'Removed', 'Content', a label and a detail line, and none of them clickable (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:211-226). A row is a destination: click it to switch to that page and select the element. Having found that a section was removed from /pricing, nobody should have to leave Compare, change page and find it by eye. The comparison is only useful if it ends on the canvas.

rows.why: UX-I-20 second half — there is no conflict state, and there must not be a second drawing of one: 807:6965 already draws it and is correctly marked [not-implemented]. Say what this family does and does not claim.
rows.text: One pane. The current page is blended over the approved one and a slider moves between them, so a change reads as a shift when you scrub. Nothing is tinted or outlined — the frames are sandboxed and cannot be marked up. CONFLICT (UX-I-20): Compare has no notion of 'the client approved v3 while you were editing' — the two sides are always presented as different, never as competing. That state is drawn once, on 807:6965, and is marked [not-implemented] because nothing can produce it: the only conflict code is OTEngine, engine-internal and behind the off-by-default collab flag. This family shows drift, not conflict, and must not grow a second conflict drawing.
rows.expect: One pane. The current page is blended

rows.why: UX-I-20 — the decision footer goes on the drift boards only. This board has no drift to decide about; saying so stops the footer being applied here by pattern-matching.
rows.text: Identical, so say so and stop. An empty diff view that renders two blank panes reads as broken. NO DECISION FOOTER (UX-I-20): the drift boards — side-by-side, overlay, list, single-page — end on 'Send these changes for approval / Publish anyway / Dismiss'. This one has nothing to decide, so it keeps a single Back and nothing else. An action row offering to send zero changes for approval is worse than no action row.
rows.expect: Identical, so say so and stop.

rows.why: UX-I-19 corroboration — this board was already SUPERSEDED by 158:2 on 2026-09-02, which is the same decision UX-I-19 asks for, taken once already. Name it as the precedent.
rows.text: Re-sending kills the old link (contract §1.4). Her comments carry over; only the link changes — and both halves of that must be on the confirm. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02 by 158:2: ApprovedCompareView has no re-send at all and ReviewTab.tsx:839 owns the confirm. This is UX-I-19's decision already taken once — one confirm, one owner. The ReviewBar's second Re-send is the copy of it that is still live.

rows.why: List mode names every change and none of them is clickable — the rows are plain divs (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:211-226). Making the row a destination is the finding's fix. 'Compare · single-page' is the in-family destination that means 'this change, on its own page'; the full fix in code is switch-page-and-select-element, which no board can express on its own.
rows.name: hotspot/change-row → that page

rows.why: History's approval band emits UI_PANEL_OPEN {panel:'review', screen:'compare'} and lands the user in another module (SavesChrome.tsx:129-138, TabRouter.tsx:226-236). Today the prototype does not draw that edge at all, so the cross-module jump the finding is about is invisible on the boards. Drawing the inbound edge makes the jump inspectable; the RETURN address is the second half and is specced below.
rows.name: hotspot/compare-with-current → Compare

rows.why: Two independent answers to 'what changed since approval' ship. The publish gate computes its own page-level diff and lists page names with a bare edited/added/removed, capped at six (StaleApprovalModal.tsx:38-50,162-181); Compare computes a typed, itemised diff with side-by-side and overlay rendering (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:113-116, compareApprovedToCurrent). The gate is the moment the decision is actually made and it shows the weaker of the two with no door to the stronger one.
rows.name: hotspot/see-what-changed → Compare

rows.why: UX-I-21 — the Review section draws Compare's load-error at 280 (drawer) while section 17 draws the whole Compare family at 1080 (canvas surface). Two mountings for one screen, with nothing saying which is the proposal. Record that 1080 is the fix and 280 is today's code, and file the 700-vs-560 expanded-drawer conflict rather than resolving it.
rows.name: Review · compare · load-error — panel-mounted; ApprovedCompareView renders inside the Review drawer, 280 collapsed / 700 expanded (ReviewTab.tsx:497-532). UX-I-21: this 280 board records what the CODE does today; the proposed fix is the §17 Compare family, drawn 1080 wide on the canvas surface. Redraw here when the fix lands. OPEN: SPEC-NAVIGATION proposes 560 for the expanded drawer; SPEC-PAGES-PANEL, SPEC-PUBLISH-PANEL and LeftSidebar.tsx:586-587 are 700 — drawn 700, 560 unresolved.

rows.why: UX-I-21 — same inconsistency, sibling state. Left un-noted it reads as a settled 280 mounting.
rows.name: Review · compare · loading — panel-mounted at 280 collapsed / 700 expanded (ReviewTab.tsx:497-532). UX-I-21: this board records the CURRENT drawer mounting; the proposed fix is the §17 Compare family at 1080 on the canvas surface, where Compare is already drawn.

rows.why: UX-I-26 — the board already carries the defect. What is missing is the recommendation and its cost: a per-row reply needs a parentId the schema does not have, so it is design-ahead rather than a redraw of this band.
rows.name: [not-implemented] Review · reply-composer band — comments are flat (no parentId in the schema) and a reply is filed against the round's FIRST comment's page, not the one being answered (ReviewTab.tsx:242). UX-I-26: the fix is a reply per comment, inline on the row where Resolve already sits — not one global box over a grouped list. That needs a parentId (or at minimum the row's own pageId) on the comment, so it is design-ahead: see '[design-ahead] Review panel · per-comment reply'.

rows.why: UX-I-18 — this is the screen the bar's argument-less Re-send actually produces. The defect is filed on the editor side and its consequence is drawn on the client side, with nothing linking them. Cross-link so the dead-link family names its own cause.
rows.name: Client sign-off · F · dead-link · not-found · 1280 — echo of 1:6 canonical 1736:8397, which is also 1280×720. Kept because Figma rejects cross-page NAVIGATE and the editor prototype must reach this state. UX-I-18: this is also the screen a ReviewBar Re-send produces — it calls the shell with no client email, so the new round ships token: null, the old link is already revoked, and the editor reports success while the client's link resolves to nothing.

rows.why: UX-I-18 — the same cross-link as the 1:3 echo, applied on the CANONICAL board. 1339:7214's own name states that 1736:8397 is the canonical of this state on page 1:6; editing only the echo would leave the canonical silent.
rows.name: APPEND to whatever the current name is: " UX-I-18: this is also the screen a ReviewBar Re-send produces — it calls the shell with no client email, so the new round ships token: null, the old link is already revoked, and the editor reports success while the client's link resolves to nothing."

rows.why: The panel computes the user's role and spends it in exactly one place — Send for review's disabledReason (ReviewTab.tsx:146,479). Resolve, Reopen, Reattach, Revoke/Withdraw and Re-send all render live for a VIEWER and are refused by the server after the click. The pattern the codebase already uses (a named disabled reason) sits two lines away. A control that is live for someone who cannot use it is worse than one that is visibly shut.
rows.detail: UX-I-22

rows.why: One reply box at the foot posts against comments[0].pageId, so an answer to the third comment attaches to the first comment's page. The recommendation is a reply per comment, inline on the row the way Resolve already is. It is marked [design-ahead], not [not-implemented], because the blocker is a schema field rather than a missing renderer — apply-truth-marks' three markers make exactly this distinction and collapsing them loses it.
rows.detail: UX-I-26

Canvas · keyboard, zoom and viewport (one owner each)

nodes.v: Canvas · keyboard, zoom and viewport — one owner each

Tab is captured to cycle elements and preventDefault is called (Canvas.tsx:660, useCanvasKeyboard.ts:87-107); Escape only clears the selection. The documented exit, F6, is printed in neither help screen, and the skip link is called “Skip to Canvas”. Either let Tab leave — the arrow keys already traverse elements — or print the escape chord on the region and in both help screens. (UX-F-18)
One zoom owner · one step · one clamp

The footer flyout adds a fixed 10 (Canvas.tsx:408-414); the floating bar walks the presets 10/25/50/75/100/150/200/400 (CanvasFooterToolbar.tsx:258-264); the command registry is a third. From 100%, a control labelled “Zoom in” gives 110% or 150% depending on which one you found. The clamp disagrees too: 400 in the presets and ZOOM_LIMITS, 500 in THRESHOLDS.ZOOM_MAX. (UX-F-22)
Choosing a breakpoint shows that breakpoint

onDeviceChange sets the device and never touches zoom (AquibraStudio.tsx:545-548), so Wide 1920 or Tablet 768 in a ~750px lane leaves the frame overflowing and horizontally scrolled, and nothing hints that “Zoom to fit” — behind the footer’s percentage flyout — is a second, required step. Fit on device change. (UX-F-24)

Six overlay chords bind globally and plain ⌘R toggles Rulers (CanvasFooterToolbar.tsx:271); ⌘B and ⌘' sit on the same footing. They are printed only inside hover tooltips on a floating bar, so everyone pays the cost and only the people who hovered get the benefit. Move them off keys the browser owns. (UX-F-32)
Two built surfaces with no door

useInspectorMode is read and persisted and the component that sets it renders nowhere — the mode is stuck at its stored value and the orphan also binds bare “I”, the AI panel’s key (UX-F-19). The Structure popover’s footer trigger renders only in the legacy four-tool rail, so a whole 400px surface is unreachable (UX-F-27). Give each a control or delete it.
The status footer is a door

The selection readout is read-only (StudioFooter.tsx:210-224). Clicking it reveals the element and opens Layers; and when elementDims returns null it says “not visible” instead of dropping the size with no explanation. (UX-F-34)
Tab, sub-tab and five overlay toggles persist; device and zoom are plain state and reset to Desktop / 100% on every reload, across three storage mechanisms. One rule, one store. (UX-F-23)

nodes.v: Bare letters — no modifier. AI is not here: it opens in the inspector column.

aria-selected is bound to “active AND drawer open” and the 3px accent bar renders under the same condition (LeftSidebar.tsx:137-160), so a shut drawer reports a tablist with nothing chosen. Selected and open are two facts.

selected · drawer CLOSED

not selected

rows.text: The panel's answer, and only the panel's. The message is honest and reachable — the server distinguishes this case with its own error code before it spends quota — but two other shipped AI entry points hit the same server error and show nothing at all: Pages → SEO “Write with AI” and Media → “✨ Generate” both swallow the exception, flip the label back and leave the field blank. This board is not the product-wide answer until those two carry the same two sentences.
rows.expect: Not hypothetical. A dev fallback that quietly succeeded is why AI was dead in pr

Drop the two inert glyphs and the one-option view toggle; put the Select the drawer actually needs in their place. List view and sort stay where they work — the fullpage manager.
